summary: Long-poll heartbeat saturation causing GPU attach lag in reserved pool
description:
Issue summary: Over the morning window Acme Retail reported elevated inference timeouts and large attachment delays for requests routed to their reserved capacity in us-east-1. Symptoms point to a sustained backlog of GPU attach operations caused by a large number of long-polling/keepalive client connections holding scheduler/allocator resources.

Impact: Multiple endpoints for the customer experienced p99 request attach latency degradation (baseline p99 ~180ms -> observed up to 12s), elevated 429/503 from the allocator and sporadic fallbacks to hosted variants. Customer reported increased user-facing timeouts for chat sessions and billing ramp concerns.

Environment: Production reserved pool (dedicated) in us-east-1, customer Acme Retail, steady traffic from ~08:30–11:00 local time. Non-essential background jobs were not scheduled in that window per customer note.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use the customer's traffic pattern: thousands of long-polling websocket-ish connections that issue occasional inference requests across many sessions.
2) Keep TCP keepalives high (long-lived connections).
3) Send bursts of short inference requests (short streams) with low token counts and frequent new session attachments.
4) Observe allocator slot contention and attach queue growth via serving-runtime dashboards.
logs:
- Allocator logs (2026-03-10T09:12–09:45Z): repeated 'attach_request_timeout' and 'slot_unavailable' entries for customer_id=acme-retail.
- Serving runtime trace snippets: trace=abc123: attach_wait=11.8s, kv_cache_lookup=2ms, gpu_dispatch=15ms.
- Autoscaler telemetry: measured connection_count spike + sustained attach_queue_length=~230 at peak.
- Connection table: many clients with idle_since >30m but still occupying logical session descriptors.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: long-lived connections from a subset of customer clients are saturating lightweight descriptors / scheduler entries which prevents efficient batching and delays GPU attachment for eligible requests. Autoscaler has not triggered new GPU allocation because the attach pattern appears as many low-rate long-lived sessions (low aggregated token throughput).

What we've checked: allocator health (OK), GPU utilization (low per-GPU but queueing present), serving runtime p99 queue length, network TCP metrics for connection churn. No driver crashes or OOMs observed.

Telemetry links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/allocator/attach-queue?orgId=1 (private) | related incident SUP-314159 referenced for similar attach queue patterns.

Hypotheses under test: 1) Connection descriptor exhaustion / slot stealing by long-poll sessions. 2) Autoscaler thresholds tuned to throughput rather than attach concurrency; does not scale on high-connection low-token workloads. 3) A noisy client cohort holding warm slots but not dispatching tokens, causing other requests to be deferred.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged customer report, requested customer upload of connection logs and example request IDs. Escalated to SRE. SLA timer started.

2026-03-10 09:44 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Observed attach_queue_length spike and cluster-side hold on scheduler descriptors. Low per-GPU utilization indicates attach contention vs capacity shortage. Asking customer for a list of client versions and whether clients use persistent long-polling versus short-lived connections.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (Acme Retail - Tara Lin): Confirmed recent client-side rollout included a websocket keepalive change (30m). We rolled back for one cohort and saw slight improvement. Providing sample request IDs: req-ACME-98765, req-ACME-98766.

2026-03-11 14:12 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Ran a targeted mitigation: temporarily capped per-tenant long-lived session descriptors on scheduler for Acme Retail to 10k, which reduced attach_queue by ~40% but caused a small percentage of 429s for long-lived sessions. Follow-up needed to tune backfill behavior.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirms visible improvement in p99 attach latency after rollout of a client-side fix and our temporary scheduler cap. Work remains to harden autoscaler and allocator heuristics.
2026-03-12 12:00 - Product Ops (Lena Müller): Noted pattern for product backlog: autoscaler should consider 'attach concurrency' signal in addition to token throughput. Opening RFC with infra team.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary per-tenant cap on long-lived session descriptors lowered attach queue and improved p99 attach latency. Customer rolled back a client-side keepalive change which further reduced contention. Next actions: tune autoscaler to include attach_concurrency metric, add allocator soft-eviction for idle descriptors after X idle time, and provide customer best-practice guidance for connection pooling. Full resolution pending infra change; target ETA for autoscaler heuristic update: 2026-04-02.
